case.title: Will the seasonally adjusted CPI-U all items index increase by 0.5% or more in August 2026, as first published by the BLS?
case.resolution_rule: YES if the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) Consumer Price Index news release for August 2026 reports a one-month percent change in the seasonally adjusted Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U), all items, of 0.5 percent or more, as first published in that release and rounded to one decimal place as BLS prints it. NO if the reported one-month change is less than 0.5 percent. Later revisions are ignored. The threshold is the top bucket of the Polymarket market for this print (0.5% or more), which is the same event as the Kalshi market 'Above 0.4%' (a one-decimal change strictly greater than 0.4%). The buckets of one print are mutually exclusive outcomes of one figure; they are scored as this single yes/no question, not as separate events.

evidence.title: BLS news release: Consumer Price Index - July 2026 (verbatim excerpt: opening summary paragraphs)
evidence.content:
CONSUMER PRICE INDEX - JULY 2026

The Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U) increased 0.1 percent on a seasonally adjusted basis in July after falling 0.4 percent in June, the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reported today. Over the last 12 months, the all items index increased 3.4 percent before seasonal adjustment.

The index for shelter rose 0.1 percent in July, accounting for roughly two-thirds of the monthly all items increase. The index for food also increased 0.1 percent over the month, as the index for food away from home increased 0.3 percent. In contrast, the energy index declined 1.5 percent in July.

The index for all items less food and energy rose 0.2 percent after being unchanged in June. Indexes that increased over the month include medical care, airline fares, communication, education, and recreation. Conversely, the index for motor vehicle insurance was among the major indexes that decreased in July.

The all items index rose 3.4 percent for the 12 months ending July after rising 3.5 percent for the 12 months ending June. The all items less food and energy index rose 2.5 percent over the year, following a 2.6-percent increase over the 12 months ending June. The energy index increased 14.7 percent for the 12 months ending July. The food index increased 3.0 percent over the last year.

evidence.title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement (July 29, 2026; full statement text)
evidence.content:
The Federal Open Market Committee approved the following statement for release by a 9 – 3 vote:

The Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 3-1/2 to 3-3/4 percent, in support of the Federal Reserve's dual mandate. The Committee is continuing its policy of maintaining ample reserves in the banking system.

Economic activity is expanding at a solid pace despite elevated uncertainty that owes, in part, to the conflict in the Middle East. Productivity growth and capital investment are strong. Job gains have kept pace with the workforce, and the unemployment rate has changed little.

Inflation remains elevated relative to the Committee's 2 percent goal, in part reflecting supply shocks that have driven price increases in certain sectors, including energy. The Committee will deliver price stability.

Voting against the monetary policy action were Beth M. Hammack, Neel Kashkari, and Lorie K. Logan, who preferred to raise the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point at this meeting.

evidence.title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee, July 28-29, 2026 (verbatim excerpt: paragraphs containing 'outlook for monetary policy')
evidence.content: With regard to the outlook for monetary policy, participants reiterated that their interpretations of incoming information would be a key component of their deliberations. Many participants assessed that policy tightening would likely be necessary if inflation did not decline. Some participants commented that financial conditions might not currently be sufficiently restrictive to facilitate a return of inflation to 2 percent. Various participants suggested that financial conditions had tightened over the intermeeting period and that this development was partly a reflection of strong economic growth and market expectations that the Committee would adopt a more restrictive policy stance before long. A few of the participants who favored raising the target range for the federal funds rate at this meeting judged that doing so would likely help forestall the need for a steeper and potentially more costly sequence of tightening moves at a later stage.

curation_notes.contamination: Default replay model llama3.1:8b: knowledge cutoff December 2023 (Meta model card). This 2026 event is after that cutoff, so contamination_flag = unlikely (never 'none'). Check any other model's card first. The curator (Claude, training data to about mid-2026) may itself know the answer; the mechanical rule is what stops that from steering case or evidence choice.

evidence_classification.cpi-2026-aug.cpi: Official BLS statistical release, verbatim excerpt. documentary_fact: measured price changes as first published for an earlier month (not the print being forecast; later revisions are not reflected).
evidence_classification.cpi-2026-aug.statement: Official FOMC policy statement. documentary_fact: the policy action and vote it records; analyst_interpretation: the Committee's own description of the economy, including inflation, and its forward guidance (official guidance, not a numeric forecast).
evidence_classification.cpi-2026-aug.minutes: Official minutes, verbatim excerpt. analyst_interpretation: summarized views of FOMC participants on the outlook for policy, as written by the FOMC Secretariat (not individual quotes, not a numeric forecast).
evidence_classification.cpi-2026-aug.nowcast: Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland model output, verbatim values from the archived data file. forecast: a statistical model's daily estimate of this month's CPI change, made before the release. It is not the print and carries model error.

curation_notes.excerpt_method: Verbatim. Same extraction code as #54/#67. Fed pages fetched live on observed_at; HTML tags removed, entities decoded, runs of whitespace collapsed, paragraphs joined with a blank line; each paragraph was also found verbatim (whitespace-normalized) in the archive_url capture, dated before as_of. BLS pages refuse automated requests (HTTP 403), so BLS text is taken from the archive_url capture (before as_of) of the permanent BLS archive URL; each excerpt paragraph was also found in a second pre-as_of capture of the BLS current-release page. Cleveland Fed nowcast: values copied as strings from the chart for this month in the latest pre-as_of capture of nowcast_month.json (no rounding); that capture's 'Actual CPI Inflation' values for this month were empty. The live file shows current data only, so this item is archive-only.
curation_notes.release_times: BLS: 'embargoed until 8:30 a.m. (ET)' (13:30 UTC standard time, 12:30 UTC daylight time). FOMC statements and minutes: 'For release at 2:00 p.m. EST/EDT' as printed (19:00 / 18:00 UTC). Cleveland Fed nowcast: the file states an update stamp without a time zone, so published_at = available_at = the archive capture time, a verifiable upper bound.
curation_notes.human_check: Each evidence item is listed in docs/curation/VERIFY_82.md for the finance owner's confirmation (#82). Not admitted until ticked there.

market.venue_rule_differences: Polymarket YES = one-month change of the seasonally adjusted CPI-U of 0.5% or more (one decimal). Kalshi YES = 'Above 0.4%'; the KXCPI contract terms define the Underlying as the one-month, one-decimal change in the seasonally adjusted CPI-U published by BLS, first published (revisions after expiration ignored), payout strictly greater than the level. On one-decimal values these are the same event. They differ only if BLS does not publish on schedule (Kalshi extends expiry; Polymarket's later markets wait until the next scheduled CPI release, then use the most recent previous month); rule 5 requires the release on the venues' date. Market rule text read on 2026-11-14 through the repo adapters (not stored); the KXCPI contract terms PDF read on the same day is the current version and may differ from the one in force then.
